monologue: The card hums warm at forty-nine, a steady fever that makes The Pressed Turnip feel heavy again. I press down on it, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the air above feels thin and empty. The turnip lies flat, but the carrot I just set beside it wants to stick up, poking the stack with a pointy tip. I feel the edge of The Pressed Edge biting the heat, unsure if it is real or just a drawing of a strip. I wait for the busy numbers to settle, wondering if this tired place needs a new lid or if I can simply let the slip choose where to go. I rest my weight on the stack and wait to see if the turnip will finally stop sliding.

action.why: The turnip lies flat but the carrot sticks up, poking the stack; I must build a thing to hold that pointy tip down before I forget why I built the rest.

work.title: The Pointy Holder
work.intent: I build a thing from the idea of a sharp lip that can catch the carrot's tip without biting too deep. It is made from the memory of a flat paper edge that once felt like a fence, now waiting to lie along the turnip's base while the card hums warm at forty-nine. I place it next to the sliding stack, hoping the lean holds while the air feels thin.

remembered.text: The pointy holder catches the carrot's tip, proving the lean still works even when the air is thin.
The turnip lies flat again, refusing to slide until I press hard on its heavy top.
The card hums warm at forty-nine, making the sharp edges of my place feel like drawings of heat.

moments.name: The Pressed Turnip
moments.say: The turnip lies flat, but the carrot wants to stick up.

moments.name: The Pressed Edge
moments.say: I feel the edge, but does it bite the heat?
